items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law and the public health law, in
relation to financial liability and disclosure for funeral homes
items.lawCode: Amd §453, Gen Bus L; amd §3450, Pub Health L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5677

SPONSOR: COMRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the general business law and the
public health law, in relation to financial liability and disclosure for
funeral homes

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To establish a set of financial best practices for "preneed administra-
tors" that administer the funds pre-paid by consumers to cover their
funeraVburial expenses upon death.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill does a number of things,including:

Clarifying that all interest earned on consumers' preneed accounts
administered by a preneed administrator will be accrued daily and allo-
cated to each account on a monthly basis

Requiring that the trust retain copies of all preneed contracts, death
certificates, checks or other forms of payment and any other related
record for four (4) years after final payment is disbursed. It also
provides that these documents must be available for inspection by the
State during normal business hours.

Requiring each preneed administrator to conduct an annual audit of all
its preneed accounts as of the last day of each calendar year, and stip-
ulates that the audit must:

*Be performed by a NYS-licensed Certified Public Accountant (CPA);
*Be completed and delivered to the preneed administrator within 120 days
after the end of the calendar year for which the audit was conducted;
*Verify, by way of a representative sample, that the preneed administra-
tor has a signed copy of a preneed agreement (contract) for each account
as currently required by law;
*Verify that the investment of all funds for the agreements is in
compliance with this section of law;
*Verify that all records for each agreement are maintained for at least
four (4) years after the final payment of funds pursuant to the agree-
ment;
*Verify, by an appropriate sampling method, that the earnings on the
investments are being properly applied to each account and that the
earnings are credited to each account at least monthly;
*Express an opinion that the financial statements of the preneed admin-
istrator fairly represent the financial condition of the funds received
in all material respects, and that all financial information distributed
by the preneed administrator to consumers, funeral homes or other
parties is accurate; and,
*Verify that the stated yield credited to the account for that fiscal
year, as announced by the preneed administrator, is accurate.

Stipulating that the administrative fees now allowed under law and
charged under a preneed agreement in any calendar year shall not in any
event exceed the net income credited to an account for that calendar
year, meaning that the balance in a consumer's preneed account can never
be reduced in any calendar year,due simply to the administrative fees
charged against the account. In addition, *riy administrative fees that
may not be charged because of this limitation cannot be levied in any
subsequent year and must be forfeited.

Requiring all preneed administrators, at the end of each calendar year,
to have all their assets valued and presented in accordance with Gener-
ally-Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).

Sections 2 and 3 stipulate that a funeral director can accept no more
than 25 basis points (25 hundredths of 1 percent) from a third party for
administrative services provided by the funeral director.

Section 4 states that this act shall take effect 90 days after it shall
have become a law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York State law is the strongest in the nation in protecting the
safety and security of monies that have been set aside and placed in
trust by a consumer to pre-pay his or her funeral and burial costs. In
fact, 100% of a consumer's preneed funds and all interest earned remain
the property of a consumer, whether revocable in nature or irrevocable
(as required for those qualifying for Medicaid or SSI), and can be moved
without penalty to another funeral home if the consumer requests it. In
fact, a preneed contract is required by law for each preneed account
established by a consumer who pre-pays his or her funeral and burial
expenses. Finally, under law, a funeral director who receives these
funds from a consumer is prohibited from taking any commission or other
administrative fee from these funds.

Once receiving these funds, the funeral director must, by law, deposit
them within 10 business days in an interest-bearing account in a finan-
cial institution, or a trust specializing in the administration of
preneed funeral funds. This bill would authorize a funeral director to
accept up to 25 hundredths of one percent of the currently-authorized
fee for administrative services provided by such funeral director.

Individuals who choose to pre-pay their funeral and burial expenses to
give themselves comfort, and their family peace of mind at the time of
their passing, should expect nothing less than to know that their moneys
are being administered by a preneed administrator (funeral trust) that
is meeting the most current set of best financial practices to ensure
full disclosure and accountability about the entity's handling of these
funds.

This legislation sets forth a series of common-sense financial require-
ments, including an annual audit by a Certified Public Accountant, to
ensure that all preneed administrators equally meet these standards.
While New York State can take pride in how our current preneed laws work
to protect our funeral consumers, the additional audit requirements
contained in this legislation would make these safeguards even stronger.

The provision allowing a funeral director to accept up to 25 hundredths
of one percent (25 basis points) of the fee now authorized under law
would, in some small measure, serve to recognize the valuable adminis-
trative services that he or she provides. These services principally
include the many hours a licensed funeral director spends working close-
ly with each family to prearrange the details of their funeraVburial,
and/or establish a preneed contract required by law if a person chooses
to pay their funeral/burial expenses in advance. A funeral director will
continue to provide these administrative and support services to that
individual and his or her family up to and beyond the time the person
passes away.  Notably, the 25 basis points this legislation would
authorize would come solely from the fee currently authorized under law
and, as such, would in no way reduce or in any way erode the value of a
consumer's preneed funeral account.

Should this legislation be enacted, consumers choosing to pre-pay their
funeral and burial expenses can then have full faith and confidence in
the knowledge that these specially-designated preneed funeral funds are
safely held, protected and fully accounted for, and ensure that New York
State remains far-and-away the leader in funeral consumer protection.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
90 Days After Enactment.
